outcome: The existing Vercel production workout app supports reliable Google sign-in, authenticated state storage, and a verified OpenAI-backed request without Auth.js configuration errors.
non_goals: Migrating the Neon database or altering stored user data beyond a no-op verification
constraints: Preserve all secrets outside source control and command output
Make the smallest complete auth repair
Use the existing Vercel project and production alias
Stop after three failed fix hypotheses or if a required credential is unavailable

success_checks.command_or_condition: A fresh in-app-browser Google sign-in returns to the production alias with an authenticated session and no Auth.js runtime error.
The authenticated production /api/state endpoint returns a successful JSON response backed by Neon.
One bounded authenticated production /api/ai estimate request returns model output without exposing the API key.
Vercel reports the deployment READY and no new auth, storage, or AI runtime error clusters after verification.

stop_conditions: All required success checks have fresh evidence
The same blocking credential or platform condition prevents progress three times
Three distinct repair hypotheses fail and the authentication architecture requires user review
required_evidence: Fresh unit, auth regression, and production build output
Vercel deployment ID and READY state
In-app-browser authenticated session, state API, and AI API observations
approval_boundaries: Do not reveal or commit credentials
Do not change Google Cloud OAuth credentials or authorized redirect URIs without a required user-only confirmation
Do not delete or overwrite existing workout data
Deploy only to the existing workout-app Vercel project
